title: When I Was Your Age
logline: A dad tells his kid how he got to school: miles of highland, the Blue Nile, a crumbling bridge, the Simien cliffs and the lava lake of Erta Ale. When he finally arrives, the teacher says: "You're late again!"
translation_notes: The dad's story (shots s02 to s08) is a routine he went through every school day as a boy, not one trip. Use the past habitual for his actions (for example ይመለከቱኝ ነበር, 'they used to watch me'), never a one-time past. The kid's line in s01 and the teacher's line in s08 are single moments. Write the Simien Mountains as ሰሜን ተራሮች and the park as ጨበራ ጩርጩራ.
style: Minimal hand-drawn doodle cartoon. Every person is a simple stick figure: a big round head, a thin line body, stick-thin arms and legs, heavy-lidded sleepy half-closed eyes and a sly little smirk, drawn with thin black ink lines. Faces and limbs are filled with one flat warm brown skin colour. Backgrounds are simple and flat: a muted, almost monochrome palette of pale sage green and soft grey, loose sketchy lines for bushes, hills and ground, plenty of empty space. Small flat colour accents only where the story needs them, such as orange lava or brown river water. No shading, no gradients, no detailed or painted scenery, not 3D, not realistic. No text, letters or writing anywhere.

young_dad.description: a stick-figure boy about 10 years old with a big round head that is shaved bald except for one small round tuft of black hair just above the forehead (the traditional Ethiopian kuncho hairstyle), simple shorts, barefoot, a small bundle of school books tied with string under his arm

dad.description: a stick-figure Ethiopian man of about 45: big round head, thin line limbs, short greying hair and a short greying beard, a thick white handwoven cotton gabi shawl draped over both shoulders, white trousers

kid.description: a stick-figure teenage boy of about 15: big round head, thin line limbs, short messy black hair, headphones around his neck, a grey hoodie, holding a smartphone

teacher.description: a stick-figure woman schoolteacher in her fifties with a big round head, round glasses, hair wrapped in a white scarf, a stern frown, holding a long thin stick

dad.style: a warm Ethiopian dad in his forties telling a tall tale to his teenage son: proud, playful, slightly dramatic, unhurried

kid.style: a bored, whiny teenage boy complaining

teacher.style: a stern village schoolteacher, sharp and loud, scolding

shots.reason: Sets up the moment every viewer knows before the story starts.
shots.description: A teenager slumps on a sofa with a phone, complaining. His dad leans in from the doorway.
shots.place: A modern apartment in Addis Ababa
shots.image_prompt: Two stick figures in a simple doodle living room of a modern Addis Ababa apartment: a plain grey sofa, a window, a doorway, all drawn with a few flat lines. The teenage son lies slumped across the sofa in the centre, phone held up to his face, rolling his eyes. His father, wrapped in his white gabi, leans in from the doorway just behind the sofa with one eyebrow raised, about to tell a story.

lines.speaker: kid
lines.en: Dad, school is so far. It's a ten-minute walk!
lines.spoken: አባዬ፣ ትምህርት ቤት በጣም ይርቃል። አስር ደቂቃ የእግር መንገድ ነው!
lines.spoken_from_en: Dad, school is so far. It's a ten-minute walk!

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: Ten minutes? When I was your age...
lines.spoken: አስር ደቂቃ? እኔ በአንተ እድሜ እያለሁማ…
lines.spoken_from_en: Ten minutes? When I was your age...

shots.reason: Who, where and when: the flashback begins.
shots.description: Dawn. A young boy steps out of a round thatched hut with his books tied in string. A rooster crows.
shots.image_prompt: The boy walks out of the low doorway of a round thatched tukul hut, mid-stride, seen from the side, centred in the frame, books under his arm. A rooster sleeps on a simple fence beside him. Flat pale pink dawn sky and a few doodled eucalyptus trees.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: Every morning, I would wake up before the rooster, tie my books with string, and start walking.
lines.spoken: እኔማ በየቀኑ ዶሮ ሳይጮህ እነሳና መጽሐፎቼን በገመድ አሥሬ መሄድ እጀምር ነበር።
lines.spoken_from_en: Every morning, I would wake up before the rooster, tie my books with string, and start walking.

shots.reason: Shows the distance, the part of the story that is true.
shots.description: Extreme wide shot. A tiny barefoot boy on an endless path through green hills and eucalyptus trees.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme wide shot. The boy, tiny, walks along a winding dirt path in the centre of the frame, seen from the side mid-stride, through endless rolling hills drawn as simple flat sage-green doodle curves with a few sketchy eucalyptus trees. A huge empty pale sky.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: Not ten minutes. Hours. Hill after hill, with no shoes.
lines.spoken: አስር ደቂቃ አይደለም። ሰዓታት ነው የምሄደው። ጫማም የለኝ፣ ኮረብታ በኮረብታ እየወጣሁ።
lines.spoken_from_en: Not ten minutes. Hours. Hill after hill, with no shoes.

shots.reason: The first exaggeration: the danger begins.
shots.description: The boy wades across a wide brown river, books held high over his head. A crocodile watches him.
shots.image_prompt: The boy wades through a wide flat brown river with the water up to his chest: only his head, shoulders and raised arms are above the water, holding his books high over his head with both hands. Right behind him a crocodile's eyes and snout poke out of the water, watching him hungrily. Simple doodle riverbanks with a few acacia trees.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: Then came the Blue Nile. I would hold my books over my head. There was always a hungry crocodile. I never stopped.
lines.spoken: ከዛ ደግሞ ዓባይ ወንዝ አለ። መጽሐፎቼን ከራሴ በላይ አደርግና እሻገር ነበር። ሁሌም የተራበ አዞ ይኖራል። እኔ ግን ፈጽሞ አላቆምም ነበር።
lines.spoken_from_en: Then came the Blue Nile. I would hold my books over my head. There was always a hungry crocodile. I never stopped.

shots.reason: A real Ethiopian wilderness many viewers have only heard of; elephants raise the danger after the crocodile.
shots.description: In a dense green jungle, the boy tiptoes under the belly of a giant elephant, books held tight. Black-and-white colobus monkeys watch from the trees.
shots.place: Chebera Churchura National Park, southwest Ethiopia
shots.image_prompt: Seen from the side, the boy tiptoes carefully underneath the belly of a huge elephant that stands across a jungle path, clutching his books, centred in the frame. Simple doodle jungle of tall trees and hanging vines in sage green. Two black-and-white colobus monkeys with long white tails watch from a branch above.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: Next, the Chebera Churchura jungle. Elephants used to block the path, so I would walk right under them.
lines.spoken: በመቀጠል ጨበራ ጩርጩራ ጫካ አለ። ዝሆኖች መንገዴን ይዘጉብኝ ነበር፣ እኔም ከሥራቸው አልፌ እሄድ ነበር።
lines.spoken_from_en: Next, the Chebera Churchura jungle. Elephants used to block the path, so I would walk right under them.

shots.reason: Height, and the geladas make it funny and recognisable.
shots.description: The boy climbs jagged green cliffs. Gelada monkeys with red chests sit on a ledge and watch him, unimpressed.
shots.image_prompt: Seen from the side, the boy climbs a steep jagged cliff face, both hands gripping the rock and one knee raised, his books tied on his back, centred in the frame. Simple doodle Simien mountain peaks behind. On a ledge beside him, three gelada monkeys with long shaggy brown manes and bright red heart-shaped chest patches sit watching him, bored and sleepy-eyed, not helping.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: Then I would climb the Simien mountains. The geladas just used to watch me, without helping.
lines.spoken: ከዛ የሰሜን ተራሮችን እወጣ ነበር። ጭላዳ ዝንጀሮዎች ዝም ብለው ያዩኝ ነበር እንጂ አይረዱኝም።
lines.spoken_from_en: Then I would climb the Simien mountains. The geladas just used to watch me, without helping.

shots.description: The boy hops from black rock to black rock across a glowing orange lava lake. His feet smoke.
shots.image_prompt: The boy leaps sideways through the air from one black rock to the next over a flat orange lava lake, legs spread in a big jump, books held tight, small puffs of smoke rising from his bare feet, centred in the frame. The lava is flat orange with a few black crack lines under a plain dark grey night sky.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: And then, the volcano. Erta Ale. I would jump from rock to rock over the lava. My feet were always on fire.
lines.spoken: ከዛ እሳተ ገሞራው፣ እርታሌ። ከድንጋይ ወደ ድንጋይ እየዘለልኩ ላቫውን እሻገር ነበር። እግሮቼ ሁሌም በእሳት የሚቃጠሉ ይመስሉ ነበር።
lines.spoken_from_en: And then, the volcano. Erta Ale. I would jump from rock to rock over the lava. My feet were always on fire.

shots.reason: The ending. The laugh is the anticlimax; "again" is the respect, because this was every day.
shots.description: The boy arrives at a small schoolhouse, proud, clothes soaked and dripping, smoke rising from his hair. A stern teacher stands at the door with arms crossed.
shots.image_prompt: The boy stands large in the front centre of the frame, facing the viewer, proud and smug: his shorts and body dripping with water, a puddle at his feet, and grey wisps of smoke rising from his tuft of hair. Behind him, in the doorway of a small simple doodle schoolhouse with a tin roof, the stern woman teacher glares at him with her arms crossed and a thin stick in one hand.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.en: Finally, wet and smoking, I would reach school. And every day, my teacher would say...
lines.spoken: በመጨረሻም፣ በስብሼ እና ጨሼ ትምህርት ቤት እደርስ ነበር። እና በየቀኑ አስተማሪዬ እንዲህ ይሉኝ ነበር…
lines.spoken_from_en: Finally, wet and smoking, I would reach school. And every day, my teacher would say...
